leading_positions.synthesis: Four members put the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp configuration first, two of them (Johansson from B038, Mehlig from B041) after moving there from other opening first choices. They share the view that the Z2 classification plus the HgTe observation is a mature, independently confirmed prediction-and-confirmation arc. They do not share a settled view of attribution: all four flag that Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and the three-dimensional topological-insulator work lie outside the three names, and they differ on whether a carefully worded citation (Z2 state and its first observation) resolves this or whether it is a defect that cannot be closed within three names.

Two members, including the chair, prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) after moving from other opening first choices (B006 and B047 respectively). They share the argument that the Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction is the model directly tested by the 2018 experiments, that the phenomena are widely reproduced, and that it had the broadest opening support (seven rankers). They accept that the superconducting mechanism is unsettled, that the field is about seven years past the experiments, and that Cao and other co-first authors fall outside the three names. Both list B048 as an alternative; the chair also lists B049, Eriksson B006.

Two atomic physicists keep optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) first, citing a clean two-name credit, magic-wavelength trapping as a new principle rather than a refinement, reproduction across Sr, Yb and Hg laboratories, and the pending redefinition of the second. They share the concern that it may be read as incremental after the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes and that early lattice-clock priority is not fully settled; they differ on the best second choice (Kroll lists B020 then B048, Lindroth lists B048 then B020). Both disclose atomic-physics proximity, and Kroll flags a JILA/Hall-laboratory connection.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members name one of three distinct preferred configurations (B048, B016, B049); none of the eight preferred configurations combines parts or splits the prize across ballots, and none places B038, B006, B041, B047, B020, B024, B029 or B001 in a preferred configuration.

B048, B016 and B049 each appear as an alternative in several files: B048 is named as an alternative by Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce, B016 by Danielsson, Mehlig and Olsson, and B049 by Danielsson, Johansson, Olsson and Pearce, so the three form a connected group rather than three isolated camps.

Members across fields agree that the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and the three-dimensional topological-insulator work are a genuine credit gap for B048, and that the Kane-Mele graphene model is not the material realisation because the graphene spin-orbit gap is tiny.
Members agree that the existence of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is reproduced, while the pairing mechanism is open.

Several members who opened with a different first choice (Johansson, Mehlig, Eriksson, Pearce) say explicitly that they moved because their own first choice had little committee support, and that field proximity should not carry a prize.
Optical lattice clocks have the cleanest two-person credit on the shortlist, which supporters and critics alike acknowledge.
scientific_disputes: Whether optical lattice clocks are a new discovery (the magic-wavelength principle enabling many-atom interrogation) or the best implementation of an already honoured precision-measurement toolkit after the 2005 and 2012 prizes; Kroll and Lindroth hold the first view, Johansson and Olsson voice doubts about breadth or novelty.

Whether the 2016 topological-phases prize overlaps materially with B048; supporters (Danielsson, Mehlig, Johansson, Olsson) distinguish time-reversal-invariant Z2 matter from the quantum Hall and defect-driven transitions of 2016, while Lindroth and Kroll treat it as a real cost.

Whether the committee should weigh breadth of impact across physics (argued for B048 and B016) as a criterion alongside discovery quality, or whether this conflates popularity with merit, as Eriksson, Mehlig and Johansson caution about their own colleagues' support.

Whether circuit QED (B038) is distinct enough from the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits to be considered now; Johansson ranked it first in the opening round but did not carry it into his preferred configuration.
attribution_disputes: B048: the HgTe-specific Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal sits between Kane-Mele and Molenkamp. Danielsson, Johansson and Olsson consider a citation framed on the Z2 state and its first observation adequate; Lindroth, Kroll and Pearce see it as a structural weakness that three names cannot repair.

B016: the Cao-Fatemi-Jarillo-Herrero experimental team, Dean and collaborators, and earlier continuum-model theory (Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) lie outside the credited names; Pearce and Eriksson treat this as manageable under the three-person limit.
B049: priority among early lattice-clock proposers and the JILA and Tokyo experimental teams is not settled in the supplied record, and Lindroth and Kroll rely partly on recalled history.
B047: one named person (Halzen) stands for a large IceCube collaboration whose builders and analysts are uncredited (raised by Pearce in his own statement and by Kroll).
B038: four credited names (Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf, Wallraff) compete for three places, and members use different triples (Girvin appears only in Olsson's).
B006 and B020: Metzner and the DFT+DMFT developers are outside the DMFT credit; Chu is outside the atom-interferometry names.
maturity_disputes: B048 is described by its supporters as mature, with about two decades of independent confirmation; Johansson questions whether the label 'overdue' is accurate given the credit tangle.

B016 is about seven years past the 2018 experiments with an unsettled pairing mechanism; Pearce and Eriksson would not wait, while Danielsson keeps it only as an alternative and Lindroth ranked it fifth, partly on timing.

B049 has more than two decades of confirmation, but the redefinition of the second has not yet happened; Kroll and Lindroth treat it as a timing argument in favour, while Pearce and Lindroth's own uncertainty list ask whether it is a reason to wait.
B038 is regarded as mature in impact but its timing is clouded by the 2025 prize.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (B038): theorist in superconducting circuits at Chalmers, directs WACQT, colleague of Delsing and Wilson; says he would recuse or discount his view if B038 is weighed seriously.
Kroll (B049): research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, JILA being Jun Ye's home institution; no documented collaboration with Ye or Katori, but he notes a possible recusal discussion.

Lindroth: minor disclosure for B038 because Wallraff is at ETH Zurich, where she has collaborated with a different group, and general atomic-physics proximity for B049, B020 and B029; no recusal sought.
Eriksson (B006): professional proximity through DFT and DFT+DMFT work in Uppsala; no personal tie to Georges, Kotliar or Vollhardt documented.

Pearce (chair) (B047): field proximity as an astroparticle physicist with no documented IceCube connection; his documented collaborations (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+, XL-Calibur) involve none of the credited names in B016, B048 or B049.
Olsson notes a colleague connection with Johansson at Chalmers, not candidate-related; Mehlig and Danielsson report no conflict.
questions_for_round2: B048: can a three-name citation be drafted that is accurate about who predicted what in HgTe and stays within Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, or does the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang role make this configuration unsound? Supporters should state what wording they would accept, and critics what omission would be disqualifying.

B016: is roughly seven years of independent confirmation sufficient given the open pairing mechanism, and should the citation be restricted to the prediction of magic-angle flat bands and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states rather than any mechanism?

B048 versus B016: both lean on topological and two-dimensional vocabulary and the 2016 prize; what distinguishes each from that earlier award, and is a second prize in this area acceptable in the same period as the other?

B049: does a lattice-clock prize count as a discovery or invention distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control recognition, and what is the evidentiary basis for Katori's priority over other early lattice-clock proposers?

How should the committee weigh breadth of opening support (seven rankers for B016, six for B048, four for B049) against the depth of first-place preferences, given that several members moved their vote toward the broadest candidate?
Should the disclosed flags (Johansson on B038, Kroll on B049) change how their statements are weighed, and does either member wish to recuse formally?
Does any member want to carry B038, B047, B006, B041, B020 or B024 into round 2 as a distinct configuration, and on what attribution?
summary.chair_observation: The eight round-1 files form three blocs: four for B048, two for B016 and two for B049. No bloc is dominant, and the main open questions are attribution for B048, maturity for B016 and novelty for B049. B048 and B016 are each named as the alternative of members in other blocs, so movement between them is plausible; the chair, who prefers B016, lists B048 and B049 as alternatives and has no recorded conflict in any of the three. No hidden votes are inferred.
